posts.cooked:
The play order for Dawn is Blood, Sweat, Tears, Blinding Blast, Summer, Anvil, Return, Battery, Leadership, Leadership, Assault, IIRC.

Silver Gulch goes Sustain, Stout Barrel, Water Trough, Explosives Wagon, Matthew Hayes.

You can clear two citizens on the first turn by having Visionary Enlighten Ra to draw a Staff, have Fixer Bitter Strike on Citizen to 2, and Ra play Staff and Pyre the other Citizen.  Sustain will then clear the citizens on the Environment turn.

You want to flip Dawn right away so she'll flip back after 1-2 turns, then you can just wail on her.

posts.name: LewdDolphin21
posts.cooked:
armadagon:

The play order for Dawn is Blood, Sweat, Tears, Blinding Blast, Spring, Healing Light, Anvil, Assault, Return, Leadership, Leadership, Devastating Aurora

Fixed that for you!

Edit: Forgot to include my results. I got Near Mint, victory on my second attempt. My first run I put Wrest The Mind on the Explosives Wagon and kept drawing Visionary cards in an attempt to find Telekinetic Cocoon; unfortunately, the round I had drawn the Cocoon, she played Devastating Aurora and destroyed my efforts. I also accidentally had a fifth Citizen destroyed by Matthew Hayes due to forgetting that Water Trough reduces Fire damage to Gunmen cards by 2 in addition to the damage reductions from Cover cards in play. I somehow managed to survive a few rounds after the Explosives Wagon explosion, but Citizen Anvil got played and killed the hero team.

My second attempt was a bit better, since I had learned from my mistake and focused on damaging Dawn instead of trying to wait for a Wagon victory.

When the first Citizen played was Citizen Blood, I had a huge suspicion we were going to see a Blood, Sweat, Tears, Blast opening; and funnily enough, those Citizens were played in exactly that order! The other opening I was expecting was something like Truth and Anvil to really make it tough to get damage through.

For those made upset by this start, bear in mind it could have been worse–a team of base Expatriette, Bunker, Argent Adept, and Legacy, for instance, consists of useless base powers, and you would not have ever been able to draw enough cards to get started–even if you double skip everyone's turns for double card draws, you would proceed to discard both of them due to Sweat and Tears!

The only other thing of note was that at one point I had Matthew Hayes shoot a Decoy Projection rather than hit a Citizen, which almost certainly mattered considering how close I came to flipping Dawn.

Near Mint, although I'll admit after seeing that the game started with empty hands for the heroes, I came here to read first.   When I saw the order of the day was "Hit Dawn with everything you've got, and only worry about Citizens/Environments that are really killing you," the rest became academic.  By Round 3-4, I had the Staff, Imbued Fire, and the Explosives Wagon out, so every hero was hitting Dawn for at least +2 DMG/hit; Ra (Staff) and Expatriette (Nemesis) were doing +3.  Finished her off in Round 7 with a DW Fixer Overdrive (5 pts each hit), but had 23 more points of pain in store for Dawn on the upcoming turns of Ra (Flame Strike (5 pts) + Living Conflag (4 pts) + Base Power (5 pts)), and DW Expatriette (RPG (4 pts) + Pride (5 pts)).  Could also have destroyed the Explosives Wagon on DW Expat's last turn for 4 more points, if necessary.

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

Rough start, clearly. After the initial round, though...it wasn't too bad.

I kept waiting for Devastating Auroura to come out, but it never did.  The Wagon stayed intact the whole game, too. If it had blown, I would not have made it.

The Rise with the Dawn card actually helped me keep Dawn on her front side. I was very thankful that Blood was the Citizen it took back (he had been taken out by Matthew Hayes). I Mental Divergenced it away toot sweet, though.

 

Once Tears and Sweat and Anvil were in the trash (and it didn't take long to eliminate them once the wagon and imbued fire were in play), I just kept as much focus on Dawn as I could, and she went down hard. 

I started with Visionary drawing cards for Ra, but switched to drawing cards for herself about halfway through.

Fixer had Hoist Chain out for most of the game, and Drving Mantis about 1/2 the time. I mostly had Fixer eat Ra's staves and Expat's extra submachine guns. Expat used Pride with various ammo, and Ra lit things (mostly Dawn) on fire.

 

Visionary ended at 1hp, others were in high single digits.

posts.name: JimmyTheCannon
posts.cooked:
That was a very close Near Mint. Finished with Fixer at 1 HP and everyone else incapped (so yay, achievement!) It would've been a Mint but I rewound when I accidentally played a style from Fixer's hand that I hadn't meant to play. :-(

 

I've never fought Dawn before, and I misremembered her card a round into it. I thought she'd flip at 3 citizens in the trash, so I was careful to only kill 2 initially, then was surprised when she didn't flip after the environment killed a third.

 

When she *did* flip and got 2 Citizens out (because Return with the Dawn was in play), I mistakenly left it in instead of destroying it with Visionary's incap power because I forgot she counts as a citizen and she was going to flip back next turn anyways.

The Explosives Wagon was brutal; it kept me from redirecting with Fixer (right after I played that style with him as the highest HP hero), and I had Imbued Fire out when it exploded with no Flesh of the Sun God, so it did a lot of damage. The second one scared the crap out of me; by that point Fixer was at 7 and Ra and Expat were lower, so if I took it out everyone but Fix would die and he'd be at 1, so I had to leave it alone. This was the first game I got to use Expat's Hairtrigger Reflexes, which ended up taking out the Stout Barrel the turn that it and one of the Hayes brothers came into play, but otherwise it didn't do anything. Then Mr. Hayes casually took out Expat and Ra because they were the 2 lowest non-environment targets (1 and 3, I believe).

I thought I was screwed, but Dawn ended her turn at 12 HP with Mr. Fixer at exactly 1, with Ra and Expat giving him a power use each for 3 total Bitter Strikes at 4 damage each thanks to the Wagon. Extremely, extremely close.
